chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymuli, from Amr ibn Uthman al-Azdi, from Muhammad ibn Uzafir, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:
The brisk walking (ramal) in the valley of Muhassar is a measurement of one hundred cubits.

key_terms.الرَّمَلُ: Ramal: A brisk, short-stepped walk performed by pilgrims during Hajj.
key_terms.ذِرَاعٍ: Cubits: A traditional unit of length measurement.
key_terms.وَادِي مُحَسِّرٍ: Valley of Muhassar: A specific location in Mecca associated with this ritual.

ai.seo_question: What is the defined distance for Ramal in the valley of Muhassar according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the precise geographical boundary for Ramal, limiting the brisk walking ritual to a specific stretch of one hundred cubits in the valley of Muhassar. This definition is crucial for Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the obligatory or recommended nature of Ramal from the general practice of Sa'i, ensuring pilgrims adhere to the Sunnah of the Ahl al-Bayt regarding the exact location and duration of this act.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Muhammad Al Aasimy, from Ali Bin Al Hassan Al Taymuly, from Amro Bin Usman Al Azdy, from Muhammad Bin Uzafir, from Umar Bin Yazeed,
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The brisk walking in the valley of Muhassar is of a measurement of one hundred cubits’.
en.sarwar: 8. Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-’Asemiy has narrated from Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Taymuliy from ‘Amr ibn ‘Uthman al-Azdiy from Muhammad ibn ‘Adhafir from ‘Umar ibn Yazid who has said the following: “
The distance to perform Sa‘y (running slowly) in Wadiy Muhassar is of one hundred yards.’”
